prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout UI Strings (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Key" · longest unbreakable word 206px · one-line width 206px
  col 2: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 196px
  col 3: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 184px
  col 4: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 283px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 187px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 662px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 661px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference table for comparing checkout interface strings across four languages by translation key.","reading":"Readers locate a key in the first column, then scan across the row to compare its translations; consistent row alignment helps keep those values associated.","groups":["English, 中文, 日本語, and العربية are parallel translations of the same string and should remain easy to compare across each row.","Key is the row identifier and needs enough width to distinguish entries without breaking them."],"keep_intact":["Translation keys, including their dots and underscores.","Individual words and meaningful number ranges such as 3–5 where possible."],"may_wrap":["Longer English and Arabic phrases can wrap at word boundaries.","Chinese and Japanese text can wrap naturally between characters.","Short translations can use the height created by longer translations in the same row."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [227, 125, 94, 108, 107] · table 662×441px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 36, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [227, 125, 101, 108, 100] · table 662×441px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 36, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [227, 125, 90, 119, 100] · table 662×441px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 106, 36, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
